record.paper_title: Evolutionary Dynamics of Cancer: From Epigenetic Regulation to Cell Population Dynamics—Mathematical Model Framework, Applications, and Open Problems
record.context_brief: Steady states of the heterogeneous stem-cell regeneration equation
record.original_question: Consider a nonnegative density Q(t,x) of resting-phase stem cells indexed by a one-dimensional epigenetic state x in Ω⊂R+, with effective cytokine signal Q̂(t)=∫Ω Q(t,x)ζ(x)dx. In the delay-free version of the heterogeneous stem-cell regeneration model, ∂Q(t,x)/∂t = −Q(t,x)(β(Q̂(t),x)+κ(x)) + 2∫Ω β(Q̂(t),y)Q(t,y)e^{−μ(y)}p(x,y)dy, where β, κ, μ, ζ are nonnegative and p(x,y) is a transition probability satisfying 0≤p(x,y)≤1 and ∫Ω p(x,y)dx=1 for each mother state y. At steady state, Q(x) must solve L_{Q̂}[Q](x)=2∫Ω β(Q̂,y)e^{−μ(y)}p(x,y)Q(y)dy − (β(Q̂,x)+κ(x))Q(x)=0 together with Q̂=∫Ω Q(x)ζ(x)dx. In the general case, especially when β depends on x and p(x,y) depends on the mother state y, does there exist a positive eigenvalue Q̂ with a nonnegative eigenfunction Q(x), is the resulting steady state unique, and under what conditions is it stable?

evidence.quote: The proposed mathematical framework (11) is a delay diﬀerential-integral equation that contains non-local transitions between diﬀerent epigenetic states. This type equation was not seen in most physical problems because of the principle of locality. Mathematically, there are many basic problems remain open for the equation (11).
For the simplicity, we omit the delay, and consider the equation with only one dimension epigenetic state. Hence, we have the following equation

Thus, the problem of existence and uniqueness of the steady state solution is reduced to a problem of ﬁnding a positive eigenvalue ˆQ of the operator L ˆQ so that the corresponding eigenfunction Q(x) is non-negative for all x∈ Ω.

If the transition probability p(x,y) is independent to the state of the mother cell, so that p(x,y) = p(x), the uniqueness and stability of the steady state were further discussed in [38]. However, it remains open questions for general cases. Biologically, the states of normal and precancerous correspond to stable steady states under diﬀerent conditions. Hence, mathematically identify the existence and stability of steady states are important for our understanding of the persistence of diﬀerent states.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let Ω ⊂ R_+ be a measurable set parametrizing a one-dimensional epigenetic state x. Consider the nonnegative density Q(t,x) of resting-phase stem cells governed by the delay-free heterogeneous stem-cell regeneration equation

  ∂Q(t,x)/∂t = −Q(t,x)(β(Q̂(t),x) + κ(x)) + 2 ∫_Ω β(Q̂(t),y) Q(t,y) e^{−μ(y)} p(x,y) dy,

where:
 • Q̂(t) = ∫_Ω Q(t,x) ζ(x) dx is the effective cytokine signal,
 • β: R_+ × Ω → R_+ is a proliferation rate (in general depending on both Q̂ and the epigenetic state x),
 • κ: Ω → R_+ is a death/clearance rate,
 • μ: Ω → R_+ is a mitotic loss rate (e^{−μ(y)} ∈ (0,1]),
 • ζ: Ω → R_+ is a nonnegative weighting function,
 • p(x,y) is a transition (inheritance) kernel with 0 ≤ p(x,y) ≤ 1 and ∫_Ω p(x,y) dx = 1 for each mother state y ∈ Ω.

A steady state is a nonnegative function Q(x) on Ω together with a scalar Q̂ ≥ 0 satisfying the coupled system

  L_{Q̂}[Q](x) := 2 ∫_Ω β(Q̂,y) e^{−μ(y)} p(x,y) Q(y) dy − (β(Q̂,x) + κ(x)) Q(x) = 0,
  Q̂ = ∫_Ω Q(x) ζ(x) dx.

Equivalently, one seeks a positive scalar Q̂ such that the linear operator L_{Q̂} has 0 as an eigenvalue with a corresponding nonnegative eigenfunction Q(x), normalized by ∫_Ω Q(x) ζ(x) dx = Q̂.

Questions, in the general setting where β genuinely depends on x and the kernel p(x,y) genuinely depends on the mother state y:

(i) Determine sufficient conditions on β, κ, μ, ζ, p ensuring the existence of a positive Q̂ admitting a nonnegative eigenfunction Q(x) of L_{Q̂}.
(ii) Determine sufficient conditions guaranteeing uniqueness of such a steady state.
(iii) Determine sufficient conditions under which a steady state is (locally or globally) asymptotically stable for the time-dependent evolution.

(The special case in which p(x,y) = p(x) is independent of the mother state y has been treated previously; the question concerns the general mother-state-dependent case.)
artifact.status_search_result: Available literature on the heterogeneous stem-cell regeneration framework treats the homogeneous G0 case and the special case p(x,y)=p(x) (mother-independent inheritance), where existence, uniqueness and stability of positive steady states have been established. For the general mother-state-dependent kernel p(x,y) with x-dependent proliferation rate β, no rigorous existence/uniqueness/stability theorem appears in the located sources; subsequent works rely on stochastic simulations rather than analytical proofs, and surveys explicitly list this as remaining open.

status_evidence.title: A general mathematical framework for understanding the behavior of heterogeneous stem cell regeneration
status_evidence.snippet: Steady-state analysis explicit only for homogeneous G0 model; heterogeneous case explored through stochastic simulation rather than rigorous theorems.
status_evidence.claim: No analytical existence/uniqueness/stability theorem is established for the general heterogeneous steady-state problem with mother-dependent inheritance.

status_evidence.title: Mathematical Modeling of Heterogeneous Stem Cell Regeneration: From Cell Division to Waddington's Epigenetic Landscape
status_evidence.snippet: Considers existence, uniqueness and multiplicity of positive steady states for related integro-differential evolution equations.
status_evidence.claim: Recent surveys discuss steady-state existence/uniqueness for related models, but the general mother-state-dependent kernel case remains a topic of ongoing study.

status_evidence.title: A mathematical model of stem cell regeneration with epigenetic state transitions
status_evidence.snippet: Treats uniqueness/stability under the assumption p(x,y)=p(x).
status_evidence.claim: The case where the inheritance kernel is independent of the mother state has been resolved; the general case has not.
